//: Names this repository publishes that do NOT exist on npm yet. npm Trusted Publishing (OIDC) cannot CREATE a package — it requires the name to already exist — so the first publish of a new name is a manual maintainer action needing a publish credential and an OTP, which CI does not have. An entry here IS that queued action, recorded where a reviewer sees it in the diff: before this file, the only thing carrying the requirement for #1494's `@gjsify/webview2-native` pair was a paragraph in a pull-request body, and it got done because a human remembered. It also keeps `docs/publishing.md`'s policy intact — the bootstrap is done before merge OR QUEUED as the next maintainer action — which a required gate with no escape would delete.
//readers: ONE ledger, TWO readers, deliberately not two copies. `scripts/verify-published-closure.mjs --phase pre-release` holds every entry against the WHOLE tree; it is the only reader that enumerates all of it, so it is where an entry naming a package this repo does not contain, or one that is `private` or off the release train, is refused. `scripts/check-shipped-runtime-packages.mjs` reads the same file for its two by-name ship-runtime families and adds one rule of its own: a doc that recommends depending on a pending name must say the name is not published yet.
//bidirectional: A listed name that IS published FAILS, so the list empties itself at bootstrap instead of rotting into a permanent exemption. That rot is measured, not hypothetical: an earlier draft's bidirectional arm looped over two package families only, so a declared-and-published name outside them was never re-examined and passed with exit 0 forever (#1500). The post-release phase deliberately IGNORES this file — a release does not get to declare its own gap, so a bridge that shipped pinning a name nobody bootstrapped is red on the release even though the pull request that added it was green.
//shape: Key = the npm name. Value = the queued action and who owns it. An empty value fails: an entry without a reason is an exemption, not a queued action. Empty `pending` is the correct steady state, not an oversight.

pending.@gjsify/blueprint: New public name from the ADR 0053 clause 5 flip: the published tier-1 @gjsify/vite-plugin-blueprint now depends on it, so it cannot stay `private` — verify-published-closure.mjs refuses that edge by name. OWNER: a maintainer with a publish credential and an OTP, BEFORE the release that ships it. Manual first publish, then `gjsify trust @gjsify/blueprint`; the procedure is docs/publishing.md § New `@gjsify/*` package, but take the consequence from here rather than from there. Skipping the bootstrap does NOT stall the train, and that is what makes it easy to skip: `npm:publish:prebuilt` runs `gjsify foreach --topological … gjsify publish --tolerate-untrusted-new`, which is TOPOLOGICAL and not alphabetical — measured, it emits @gjsify/blueprint before its dependent — and that flag returns `skipped-untrusted-new` with exit 0 for a name OIDC cannot create (commands/publish.ts, the OidcExchangeError 404 branch). So the loop continues and PUBLISHES @gjsify/vite-plugin-blueprint pinning a name npm does not have. It is a required `dependencies` edge and not an optionalDependency, so every consumer install of the plugin fails, on every package manager. verify-published-closure catches it in its post-release phase, which ignores this file by design — after the bad tarball is on the registry.
